warnings.warning: The prose says effective mass rises as impact moves outward, while the formula and plotted curve show it falls.
The printed continuum inertia omits cross-sectional area for volumetric density and does not consistently define point versus distributed force.
The printed ball equation equates acceleration to force without dividing by the 0.145 kg ball mass; the absent code prevents distinguishing typo from implementation.
The base Young's modulus is 1.814e10 Pa in the prose but 1.1814e10 Pa in the Figure 11 caption.
The proposed Fourier expansion prints cosine for both coefficient families instead of an independent sine phase; the shell system is not implemented.

global_organization_chain: Separate competing meanings of sweet spot and fix a speed-only operating definition
Use a rigid collision to expose recoil and local-speed intuition
Synthesize finite beam propagation with local hysteretic contact
Test timing, boundaries, limiting cases, and hysteresis by simulation
Vary material, geometry, and pitch inputs around a base wood bat
Extend the same architecture to hollow wood and aluminum shells
Explore missing hoop response with an explicitly artificial surrogate
Close with mechanism, material comparison, omitted physics, and experimental needs

main_argument_chains.claim: The speed-maximizing sweet spot is conditional and generally interior.
support_steps: Fix bat, ball, and swing conditions.
Combine momentum, angular momentum, and restitution.
Express exit speed through impact-location effective mass.
Show opposing recoil and local barrel-speed effects.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the rigid optimum only as intuition for the full transient model.

main_argument_chains.claim: Collision duration and finite wave travel reconcile rigid recoil with local vibration.
support_steps: Expose the incompatible instantaneous-rigid and locally isolated assumptions.
Couple a hysteretic ball at one segment.
Compare contact and distant-response timing plus free/fixed boundaries.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Interpret the full-model optimum through causal wave-return timing.

main_argument_chains.claim: The modeled response is mechanism-sensitive rather than a fixed bat coordinate.
support_steps: Remove hysteresis to eliminate curve crossing.
Sweep density, modulus, handle profile, and pitch speed.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Report sweet-spot location and width with operating and material conditions.

main_argument_chains.claim: Alternative-bat results are exploratory structural scenarios.
support_steps: Replace solid wood by hollow wooden shells.
Relate wider aluminum response to faster return waves.
Identify hoop response as missing and test a local oscillator surrogate.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not infer actual corking effects, material isolation, or league policy without matched real-bat tests.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Figure 2 overlays final speed, effective mass, and local swing speed to make the opposing rigid-body effects visible, although the prose misstates one direction.
Force-time and distant-displacement histories expose contact duration and causal travel time.
Full and rigid response curves plus marked rigid optima compare model hierarchy over impact position.
Paired with- and without-hysteresis plots make the ablation result visually immediate.
Aligned wood and aluminum snapshots disclose removed rigid motion and show relative wave return.
Seven frequency curves rely mainly on color-order description and lack direct labels, uncertainty, and optimum markers.
